units.function: Pure tests for canonicalizing and independently fingerprinting effective session, workspace and lease configuration while excluding volatile and sensitive values.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> effective-run-config fingerprint service -> deterministic in-memory canonicalization/SHA-256; no database, Secret provider, workspace manager, Connector runtime or attestation verifier.
units.keyDataModels: Versioned category fingerprints/canonical JSON, adapter/workspace/lease config, environment variables and resolved Secret manifest identity/version/provider outcome.
units.lifecycle: Resolve effective Run config and Secret metadata -> canonicalize each category -> hash versioned JSON -> compare with prior workspace/lease/session fingerprints -> invalidate changed reuse categories outside this suite.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 5/5. The pure suite strongly proves deterministic ordering, category-specific drift and raw Secret exclusion, but cannot prove callers classify every security-relevant field correctly or Secret providers advance versions. Adversarial canonicalization, version migration and full reuse behavior are absent.
units.designRationale: Refresh only the parts of a reusable execution environment whose effective configuration changed, without persisting raw credentials or invalidating on per-Run noise.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs secret-free, versioned runtime attestations and safe workspace/lease reuse across Connector vendors, managed cloud and local enterprise nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as a leading reference for category-specific deterministic fingerprints. Extend the attested input with Connector/protocol/binary/image/Skill/capability/data-policy/approval/Work-contract digests; require monotonic Secret versions and scoped leases; use keyed hashing or omit recoverable low-entropy value hashes; validate category completeness and version migration with compatibility tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: Fingerprints answer whether config changed, not who authorized it or which Work/data/tool/approval contract it served. Volatile Run and lease identity are excluded, so a separate signed runtime attestation must bind the concrete execution to the responsibility chain.
units.securityFindings: HIGH secret-version trust gap: changed Secret bytes under unchanged provider version deliberately produce the same fingerprint. HIGH dictionary-leak risk: ordinary env values are stored as unsalted SHA-256 hashes in canonical JSON, allowing recovery of low-entropy values and undeclared Secrets. HIGH completeness risk: sensitive-field exclusion and category placement are blacklist/caller dependent; repository URLs, commands or novel fields may retain credentials or be omitted from invalidation. Missing bindings include Connector/binary/image/Skill, capabilities/data policy, Work/approval digests and concrete Run/lease attestation.
